Nagash's Rule
The Return of the Hand
The First Legion has never been known for their strategies or elites – instead, they drown their enemies in untold numbers of expendable skeletons.
The Second Legion prefers mobility above all else, employing fast beasts, riders and chariots to terrorise vulnerable targets.
The Third Legion prefers combined-arms tactics, fielding artillery, skirmishers and cavalry, as well as binding souls from long-forgotten tombs to hold the frontlines.
The Fourth Legion has been unremarkable in their employ of regular soldiers; however, more exceptional individuals seem to arise from their ranks than in any other legion.
The Fifth Legion is infamous for its ranks of disciplined infantry and its use of terrifying monstrosities.
As the personal legion of the Dread King, the Sixth Legion has access to the most terrifying undead creations at his disposal.
Loyalty to Nagash transcends death and defeat. Cultists and undead minions gather under the Dread King's banner, leaving their forsaken hiding places to join his ranks once more.
In life, the legions received extensive training – every single one a fearsome warrior. In death, some of these memories still persist.
What they lack in accuracy, they make up for in unnatural coordination and sheer quantity.
Enchantments keep the chariots from rotting beyond use. They remain in working condition for many centuries to come.
This light cavalry was feared as opportunistic raiders in life. Their tactics have not changed much in death.
Ghouls are seen more as war-beasts than soldiers, as they lack discipline, but they make up for it in sheer ferocity.
The legions often make use of Dire Wolves and bats to terrorise soft targets.
Long ago, a mighty warrior tried to slay a vile Medusa but paid with his life for the attempt. Now, a spiteful ghost commands the corpse of the former hero.
Few mortals are foolish enough to worship Nagash as a god. All of them meet a terrible end eventually, but for some, their service to Nagash does not end with death.
Resurrected corpses are tireless workers. They need nothing and will labour until their husks fail them – but there are always more to acquire.
What followers of Nagash call a blessing, most would call a curse. Undoubtedly, there is power to be gained for those willing to pay the price.
The First Companion of the Dread King has followed him loyally and willingly into death – and beyond.
To the undead, every death is a chance to grow their ranks and expand their lands.
The intelligent undead hone their skills far beyond the physical limitations of the living.
Even unwilling souls may be forced into a necromancer's service. Spell-bound, they are made to turn their wrath towards the enemies of the master who controls them.
Long before the reappearance of the Dread King, there were rumours of dark riders haunting the lands during Hexensnacht. Sometimes such rumours are true.

Unlike the Tomb Kings, these mummies were not preserved with the intent to awaken in a utopian afterlife. Instead, they are cursed to suffer eternally as puppets, used to further the ambitions of their dark master.
There is strength in numbers – sheer, unlimited numbers therefore equal almost unlimited strength.
Even the artillery deployed by the legions is forged from the cursed remains of unlucky beings, animated by the malicious intent of a necromancer.
In ancient times, only nobles would ride into battle on chariots. Now long dead, they still retain a fraction of their superior training.
Long ago, these javelins were used to hunt elephants or giant vultures of the deserts.
Those with superior speed and manoeuvrability dictate the time and place of engagements – being faster than the enemy is paramount for success.
‘How cruel life is that you breathe while I must rot. Crueller still am I, for I shall rectify matters.’ – Marquis of Mullyn, Hellwraith
Sometimes, those who venerate the gods of death find their path leading into the employ of Nagash himself – for he is the true master of death.
Some say this Companion did not willingly accept his undeath. The choice, however, was not his to make, and now he serves the Dread King anew in death.
Wraiths harbour malicious intent towards all living beings. Most necromancers deem this useful, as it provides the spectres with additional motivation when facing their master's mortal enemies.
Not all liches of the Mortuary Cult oppose Nagash. Some see him as the greatest of their kind and serve him willingly in exchange for some of his secrets.
Bound to the will of their master, most ghosts are completely mad. There is no reasoning with such a foe.
Fallen in ancient times, his remains were carefully preserved for the time when his king would call him to service once again.
Curiosity for the dark arts inevitably leads down a grim path.
Sometimes, when the purple wind blows strongly, wraiths will appear without the need for a necromancer to summon them against the living.
Said to have achieved undeath even before his master, he loyally guarded the Dread King's tomb while his liege was regenerating.
Shields linked, ranks closed and spears forward – discipline and training made these Wights strong in life and now terrifying opponents in death.
The charge of this heavy cavalry strikes fear into the enemy's ranks.
With the length of their pikes, enemies can be kept at a safe distance.
These ghostly apparitions exist only to reap the lives of as many beings as they can.
Ancient cursed treasures and the possessions of the recently deceased are used to further the Dread King's cause.
Only a balanced army can be prepared for every possible threat.
This artillery and its grotesque ammunition are designed to break both body and spirit of the opposition.

It is said that in ancient times, a long-forgotten hero descended into a labyrinth near Khemri inhabited by a clan of vicious Minotaurs and slew almost all of them before falling himself. This may just be a legend, but it could explain where the legions get their grisly supply of Minotaur bones.

When an elephant is dying, it has the habit of seeking out a special place to die among the remains of its already deceased ancestors. Finding such a place gives a necromancer convenient access to their bones.
The walking dead will take everything from the living – even their chance for an afterlife.

Once, a famous hero entered a labyrinth to slay a small group of Minotaurs. He very nearly succeeded, but the leader of the beasts struck him down. Now, his corpse is puppeteered by a vengeful spirit.
One champion can be worth hundreds of lesser soldiers – therefore the talentless must serve as stepping stones to further the strength and development of the gifted.
Lured by dark promises, Haptmose, the Liche High Priest known as the Traitor of Mahrak, has forsaken his fellow Tomb Kings to enter the service of Nagash.
The dead never retreat – wherever they set foot, the land becomes the property of Nagash.
The wicked labrys is a fearsome weapon, especially when wielded by merciless Wights.
It is said this Companion loved battle so much that he sees his undead form as a blessing, for he may continue to fight indefinitely.
Many ghosts enjoy frightening the living; however, this one tends to do much more harm than merely scaring them.
The endpoint of a successful necromancer's journey is always ascension into an intelligent undead. The Dread King has use for such individuals.
King Nebwaneph has been convinced by the traitor Haptmose to turn on his fellow Tomb Kings and swear loyalty to Nagash.
Pikes and spears will hold the line while monsters and artillery lay waste to our enemies.
Only the best javelin-throwers may become royal peltasts – superior in both skill and equipment.
Hydras prey upon elephants and therefore can often be found near elephant graveyards. Once slain, they make a fine addition to the Dread King's legions.
Some left the Mortuary Cult to side with Nagash when he first rose so many centuries ago; others fall to temptation later when trying to unlock the secrets of his magic.
Not all wraiths are corrupted when first bound, but malicious madness will inevitably follow.
Fallen and unburied on a forgotten battlefield in the deserts, sand and heat preserved this Companion until his king returned and raised him for unholy duty once more.
King Omanhan III has been swayed by the honeyed words of the High Liche Priest of Mahrak to join forces with the Dread King in the name of Nagash.
Only the best soldiers and darkest magic can guarantee victory.
The mere presence of a Mortis Engine drains the life force from nearby enemies.
The legions were infamous in their own right and have seen more battlefields than even most of the oldest Elves.
Chariots were once feared across the land – and so it shall be again.
Many knights fancy themselves the best alive, but all pale before the dead.
Some souls hold greater power than others, but all can be forced to serve with sufficient will.
Stab them with the pointy end and keep them away from you – simple, but brutally effective.
These lands have been tainted beyond measure, and Shyish blows strongly here. Only the foolish or the desperate would dare to enter.
Nagash's secrets are his own, but sometimes granting a few morsels of power to a loyal servant makes them more useful.
The colossal remains of a forgotten race of giants are difficult to reanimate and control, but their sheer power is worth the effort.
The accuracy of the undead is often not as good as that of their living counterparts; however, with enough projectiles, they are almost guaranteed to hit something.
Ghouls and beasts can swarm the enemy backlines and sow confusion and fear while more valuable troops make their move.
Superior horse archers in life, nomads of the Arabyan deserts make for excellent undead skirmishers too.
The unholy artillery used by the legions is a horrifying sight to behold – each a cursed undead construct in its own right.
Already feared in life, these reanimated remains of the monsters of the great deserts are no less terrifying.
Where the servants of Nagash go, death – and worse – follows.
Nagash will rule everything and everyone with supreme authority – in due time.
What is already dead cannot be killed permanently – another legendary servant of Nagash returns from defeat to serve his master once more.
